sections.html:
Madison County Tax Administration is in Room 25 at 5707 Highway 25/70 in Marshall, phone 828-649-0734. Posted hours are weekdays, 8:00am to 5:00pm, and the office is closed Saturday and Sunday.

The job is split three ways. The assessor lists and values property, the county commissioners choose the rate, and a separate tax collector sends and collects the bills. Take a rate complaint to the commissioners and a value complaint to the assessor.

A Marshall town lot and a steep mountain tract sit on the same roll yet look nothing alike, so read your own parcel record before an offer arrives.

The county-wide rate is 0.36 per $100 of value, with a fire district charge added for each parcel and a town charge where one applies. The figures below are the 2024-2025 rates. Ask tax administration for the sheet that matches your own bill.

Ten fire districts are listed, running from Laurel at the low end to Leicester at the high end. A solid waste line follows: 180.00 per household for residential, 29.00 after subsidy for elderly or disabled households, and a fee schedule for commercial users. The full list is on the Madison County tax rates page.

sections.h2: How the assessor sets a value
sections.html:
Three methods feed one number: cost, income and market. The assessor weighs what sellers and buyers have been doing and what construction costs, then settles on an assessed value for the parcel.

Land and buildings stay on the roll without re-listing. A homeowner reports only changes, such as an added garage or a demolished shed. Personal property gets listed each January, including single-wide mobile homes, boats, farm machinery, unlicensed campers and unregistered vehicles.

  • The county contracts outside help for its periodic reappraisal.
  • Ownership changes and parcel maps are kept by the assessor.
  • A GIS system shows boundaries and aerial photography.
  • New structures need an E-911 address before a building permit issues.

Compare the record with what you actually own. An outbuilding missing from the card, or the wrong acreage, is simpler to correct now than in the middle of an inspection period.

Bills are payable from September 1, and face value is accepted into early January. After that a penalty clock runs.

  • January 1 to 31: listing window for personal property.
  • September 1: bills due.
  • January 6: a 2 percent charge is added.
  • February 1 onward: three-fourths of one percent more, monthly.

For mail, the postmark date is the payment date. Early-payer discounts are optional for counties and towns, so ask tax administration whether one is in force. The office's page also links to online payments.

Complete the county's formal appeal form and send it to the Madison County Assessor's Office, 5707 US 25/70, Suite 3 Box 4, Marshall, NC 28753. The 2026 version asks for your value opinion as of January 1, 2024.

Expect questions on when you bought and for how much, the year built, fire insurance coverage, any inheritance or family sale, and improvements with their costs. Attach an independent appraisal if one exists. A house on the market needs the asking price and the broker's agreement attached, and rental property needs its latest three years of income and expense figures. Anyone filing for an owner submits an assessor-approved, notarized power of attorney.

A bigger bill is no ground for appeal. Argue the value, using comparable sales and repair estimates.

Above the assessor sits the board of equalization and review, usually the commissioners themselves, which convenes in a window running from the first Monday in April to the first Monday in May. Request your hearing before it adjourns. Once its decision is mailed, the state Property Tax Commission is the next stop, with 30 days to file.

Madison County offers an elderly and disabled exclusion, an agricultural and forestry land use program and other exemptions. An owner may draw on only one of the three state programs below.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: shields the larger of $25,000 or 50 percent of appraised value. Applicants are 65 or over, or permanently and totally disabled, with income at or under the 2026 cap of $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income test on the form.
  • Circuit breaker: a 4 percent of income ceiling, rising to 5 percent when income falls between $38,800 and $58,200 (2026 numbers). Owners must have lived there five years.

File Form AV-9 with the county assessor, who must take it through June 1. Circuit breaker applicants file again every year. The form is on the NCDOR Form AV-9 page.

The debt stays with the land. G.S. 105-355 attaches the lien at the listing date, penalties, interest and costs included, and the title agent will want it cleared when keys change hands.

Circuit breaker owners face one more item. Deferred tax from the previous three fiscal years comes due on a transfer, on the owner's death, or when the owner moves out. Madison County asks attorneys and paralegals for 10 days' notice so tax administration can produce deferred bills, which means a rushed closing can stall on paperwork.

Long-unpaid tax can end in a court foreclosure and a public auction, and tax administration's page links to those sales. Redeeming ahead of confirmation takes full payment of tax, penalties, interest and costs.

sections.h2: What a seller can do before listing
sections.html:
Madison County has about 22,553 residents, and many are long-settled families, which produces back taxes, inherited mountain land and tired houses. These steps help in each case.

  • Request a statement for every parcel, with any deferred amount.
  • Check that the tax record and the deed show the same owner name.
  • Find out which relief or land use status the buyer would inherit.
  • Commission a survey first if the acreage is in doubt.

A cash buyer can settle the tax balance from the proceeds and skip the repair list, which fits owners who want out of an overdue parcel. Closing then follows a short path: the buyer's attorney requests the payoff, the title agent confirms any deferred bill, and the tax is paid from proceeds before the deed is recorded. The same 10 day notice applies, so call tax administration at 828-649-0734 as soon as you have a buyer.

faqs.q: Who answers questions about Madison County property tax?
faqs.a: Call Madison County Tax Administration at 828-649-0734 or stop by Room 25, 5707 Highway 25/70, Marshall. It posts weekday hours, 8:00am to 5:00pm.

faqs.q: Which towns have their own rate in Madison County?
faqs.a: Marshall (0.355), Mars Hill (0.47) and Hot Springs (0.45) each add a charge on the 2024-2025 sheet. The 0.36 county rate covers every township.

faqs.q: Will a larger bill alone win an appeal in Madison County?
faqs.a: No. The 2026 form says a rising bill is not a valid reason. Your case must be about market value on the valuation date shown.

faqs.q: When does Madison County start charging interest on unpaid tax?
faqs.a: It begins on January 6 with a 2 percent charge. Beginning February 1, three-fourths of one percent more accrues monthly.

faqs.q: Can a Madison County owner close a sale with tax still due?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien gets paid from your proceeds at closing. Ask the tax office for a payoff early, and allow 10 days if deferred bills must be prepared.
